title: Called up for the draft and then exempted
summary: Leeman gives up his Woody Herman job and apartment for induction at Fort Dix, but a new rule exempts fathers over thirty and he does not go.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Uh huh. Now what years are we talking about now, Cliff? I just wanted to clarify that.
Well, we can go back over lots of things, but ... I was taken in the draft, to go into the Army, so I had all these songs that became so great with Woody -- I had rehearsed, like --
Well, you went in the Army and ...

I rehearsed all these things -- I was going to Fort Dix on a Monday, two weeks previous, so I had to give up my job. Woody had gone and hired Davie Tough who was not quite ready to go to work, he had just gotten out of the Navy, he was down in the South Pacific, and was in bad condition -- but he hired Dave to follow me, he hired Dave, and I gave up my apartment in New York, and my first wife had gone to Boston with my son, who had just been born then. He was a young baby. I had no apartment, I had no job, and I got through with Woody on a Saturday night, and on Sunday, the papers were headlines, it said all fathers over 30 years old were exempt from the draft -- and I was just over 30, with a baby.
So you didn't have to go.

I didn't have to go in the Army. I didn't go. Monday morning I was to go to Fort Dix; I had my induction. But I had no apartment, my wife and son had gone out of town to Boston to live, and I had no place to live -- I moved into a hotel, and I had no job. What else can I say?
